The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)},$$
and extend linearly. This definition is valid for every $\delta\in\mathbb C$, including $\delta=0$.

For $m,n\in\mathbb N$, the subspace of **negligible morphisms** is
$$\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)= \{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n): \operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0\text{ for every }g\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(n,m)\}.$$

For arbitrary primitive $A$, write $A=A_0^k$ with $\gcd(k,4r)=1$. For each fixed pair of object labels, the matching set is finite by [F2], so the Hom spaces and trace-pairing matrices are finite-dimensional. The field automorphism preserves the ranks and kernels of all these matrices, the exact boundary ideal, and the quotient's simple labels. This completes the canonical-to-arbitrary-root transport and the proof.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D_0$ and $D_1$ be finite integral framed-link surgery diagrams in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, with surgery results $M_0$ and $M_1$. Then $M_0$ and $M_1$ are orientation-preservingly diffeomorphic if and only if $D_0$ and $D_1$ are related by a finite sequence of ambient isotopies, framed handle slides, and additions or deletions of split $\pm1$-framed unknots.

Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, the BHMV semisimplified category, and its quantum dimensions $d_j$ and twists $\theta_j$ for $0\le j\le r-2$. Put $\Omega_p=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_jp_j$, $\Delta_+=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j$, and $\Delta_-=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j^{-1}$. The Statement asserts that both $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are nonzero. For a finite integral framed link $L$ in the oriented three-sphere, color each surgery component by $\Omega_p$ and normalize the bracket evaluation by $\Delta_+^{b_+(L)}\Delta_-^{b_-(L)}$, where $b_\pm(L)$ are the positive and negative indices of the framing matrix. With the stated BHMV root and weighted anomaly convention, the resulting value is unchanged under framed isotopy, handle slides, and addition or deletion of a split $\pm1$-framed unknot.

For the fixed root parameter, the normalized double-handlebody pairing on the admissible spine states of a marked handlebody is nondegenerate after quotienting by its radical. The inverse pairing defines the sewing map for gluing along a closed marked surface, and these maps satisfy the stated weighted Lagrangian anomaly correction.

Assume full AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the surface intersection and boundary-kernel duality suppliers.

An object is a closed oriented surface $\Sigma$ with a fixed finite collection of marked points carrying simple labels of the complex modular ribbon fusion category and pairwise disjoint oriented embedded interval germs through those points (the ribbon-end arcs), together with a Lagrangian subspace $\lambda\subset H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb R)$ for the signed intersection form. An elementary morphism is an oriented compact smooth 3-bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ with product collars and fixed boundary parametrizations, a properly embedded colored ribbon graph whose ends match the marked labels and, in the fixed product collars, are exactly the products of those ribbon-end arcs with the collar interval, and an integer weight $n\in\mathbb Z$. Boundary parametrizations preserve these oriented arc germs. Reversing a boundary orientation dualizes its labels and reverses its oriented ribbon-end arcs. Composition glues the identical product ribbon germs through the common parametrized surface, with no interpolating twist.

For any closed oriented surface $\Sigma$, the intersection convention is $\omega_\Sigma([\alpha],[\beta])=$ the signed intersection number in which the tangent to $\alpha$ followed by the tangent to $\beta$ gives the surface orientation. For a bordism $M:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$, write $j_r$ for the inclusion maps into $H_1(M;\mathbb R)$ and set

$$\Lambda_M=\{(x_0,x_1)\in H_1(\Sigma_0;\mathbb R)\oplus H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R):j_0x_0=j_1x_1\}.$$

Give the product the form $-\omega_{\Sigma_0}\oplus\omega_{\Sigma_1}$. The boundary-kernel lemma applied to $\partial M$ gives the relation with $j_0x_0=-j_1x_1$; changing the sign of the second coordinate is symplectic and gives exactly $\Lambda_M$. Hence $\Lambda_M$ is Lagrangian ([[lem-3-manifold-boundary-kernel-is-lagrangian]]).

For composable bordisms $M_1:\Sigma_0\to\Sigma_1$ and $M_2:\Sigma_1\to\Sigma_2$, put $A=\Lambda_{M_1}$ and $B=\Lambda_{M_2}$. For a relation $R\subseteq\overline V\oplus W$, write $R(L)=\{w:\exists v\in L,(v,w)\in R\}$ and $R^t(Q)=\{v:\exists w\in Q,(v,w)\in R\}$. These use the inclusion maps into each individual bordism. The three Lagrangians for composition lie in the middle surface:

$$K_1=A(\lambda_0),\qquad K_0=\lambda_1,\qquad K_2=B^t(\lambda_2)\quad\subseteq H_1(\Sigma_1;\mathbb R).$$

They are Lagrangian by [[lem-lagrangian-relation-sends-lagrangian-to-lagrangian]], applied also to the transposed relation. With the Wall-form sign fixed in [[lem-maslov-index-four-lagrangian-cocycle]], define

$$n(M_2\circ M_1)=n_2+n_1+\mu(K_1,K_0,K_2).$$

For mapping cylinders of symplectic maps $f_1,f_2$, the index is $\mu(f_1\lambda_0,\lambda_1,f_2^{-1}\lambda_2)=\mu(f_2f_1\lambda_0,f_2\lambda_1,\lambda_2)$. This is Walker's prescribed sign and order. For arbitrary bordisms, replacing the individual relations by homology maps into the glued manifold is not part of the definition.

Identity bordisms are cylinders with the product ribbons on the specified arcs and weight zero. Disjoint union takes the disjoint union of geometric data, the direct sum of the surface Lagrangians, and the sum of weights. The empty surface is the monoidal unit. Bordisms are identified by orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms respecting collars, parametrizations, ribbon data and weights; smoothing glued collars is understood up to these identifications. Associativity and the weight, unit and disjoint-union laws follow from the relation identity in [[lem-maslov-correction-composes-for-lagrangian-relations]] and the proof below. Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad \delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

derivations.claim: Here $r=3$, $q=-A^2$ has $q^2$ of order three, and $q+q^{-1}=-1$. Thus $\delta=-1$, $[2]=\delta=-1$, and $[3]=\delta[2]-[1]=(-1)(-1)-1=0$.

The recursion for $p_3$ requires division by $[3]$. Since $[3]=0$ in $\mathbb C$, no multiplicative inverse exists, so this recursive expression is undefined. In particular, cancellation cannot assign it a value. The calculation refutes the asserted universal continuation; it makes no claim that a projector at rank three cannot be constructed by a different method.

Let $p\ge4$ be even, let $A$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity, and use the quantum integers and Temperley–Lieb loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ specified above. Write $r=p/2$. The standard Jones–Wenzl recursion defines nonzero idempotents $p_n$ for $0\le n\le r-1$; their unnormalized closure traces are $[n+1]$. In particular, $p_{r-1}$ has trace zero and is negligible, while the next standard recursive formula for $p_r$ is undefined because its denominator is $[r]=0$. This statement concerns that recursion and does not assert that no differently constructed normalized idempotent can exist at rank $r$.

Let $p\ge4$ be even, $A\in\mathbb C$ a primitive $2p$-th root, and $r=p/2$. In the BHMV Temperley–Lieb quotient with loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and planar pivotal trace, the complete simple-label set is $\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}$, represented by the surviving Jones–Wenzl projectors $p_a$ obtained from the standard recursion using unit denominators $[2],\ldots,[a]$. Every simple is self-dual. Its fusion multiplicities are

$$N_{ab}^{c}=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,\,2r-4-a-b) \ \text{and }a+b+c\text{ is even},$$

and are zero otherwise. With the BHMV overcrossing map $c_i=A1_i+A^{-1}U_i$, where $U_i$ is the cup-cap generator, the full-framing ribbon structure has planar quantum dimensions $d_a=[a+1]$ and simple-object twists $\theta_a=(-1)^aA^{a(a+2)}$. Here the quantum integers use the fixed BHMV recurrence. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix, whose $(a,b)$ entry is the pivotal trace of the double braiding on $p_a\otimes p_b$, is nondegenerate. Here modular means that this finite semisimple ribbon category has an invertible unnormalized Hopf-link matrix.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. Identify
the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, where $\mathcal A$ is a planar
annulus. A simple closed curve is called essential if it does not bound a disk
in $\mathcal A$. Every framed link in this product admits a regular annular
diagram and an integer framing correction from its blackboard framing. Let
$z$ be one blackboard-framed annular core curve, and for $n\geq1$ let $z^n$
denote $n$ parallel copies of that curve, with $z^0$ the empty link. In the polynomial
ring $R[z]$, $z$ is also the formal variable sent to the core class $[z]$.
Then the classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, form an $R$-basis of
$\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$. Equivalently, the map
$J:R[z]\to\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$ sending $z^n$ to $[z^n]$ is
an $R$-module isomorphism.

For the fixed root parameter, the normalized double-handlebody pairing on the admissible spine states of a marked handlebody is nondegenerate after quotienting by its radical. The inverse pairing defines the sewing map for gluing along a closed marked surface, and these maps satisfy the stated weighted Lagrangian anomaly correction.
